questions.stem: Which lights does a 25 m sailing vessel show when underway under sail alone?
options: Masthead light, sidelights and sternlight
Sidelights and sternlight
An all-round white light and sidelights
A tricolour lantern at the masthead
questions.explanation: Rule 25(a) gives a sailing vessel underway sidelights and a sternlight, with no masthead light. The masthead light is a power-driven signal, and the tricolour is only allowed for sailing vessels under 20 m.

questions.stem: At night you see two all-round lights in a vertical line near the top of a mast, red over green, with sidelights lower down. What is she?
options: A vessel engaged in fishing
A vessel not under command
A pilot vessel on duty
A sailing vessel underway
questions.explanation: Rule 25(c) allows a sailing vessel to add all-round red over green at or near the masthead ("red over green, sailing machine"). Fishing vessels show red over white or green over white, a pilot vessel shows white over red, and not under command is red over red.

questions.stem: A 12 m sailboat uses a tricolour lantern at her masthead. Can she also switch on the red-over-green all-round lights?
options: Yes, but only in restricted visibility
Yes, they are always optional extras
No, the red-over-green lights may not be shown together with the combined lantern
No, red over green is reserved for vessels over 20 m
questions.explanation: Rule 25(b) allows the tricolour on a sailing vessel under 20 m, and Rule 25(c) says the red-over-green lights shall not be shown in conjunction with that combined lantern. Red over green is not limited to vessels over 20 m.

questions.stem: A 5 m sailing dinghy and a 4 m rowboat are out after dark. Neither can practicably show sailing lights. What does Rule 25 require of each?
options: Nothing, because both are under 7 m
A masthead light and sidelights
A red all-round light
An electric torch or lighted lantern showing a white light, ready at hand and shown in time to prevent collision
questions.explanation: Rule 25(d) says a sailing vessel under 7 m shows sailing lights if practicable, and a vessel under oars may show them; if they do not, each must have a white torch or lighted lantern ready at hand to show in time to prevent collision. Neither is simply exempt, and masthead or red lights would give a false picture.

questions.stem: By day you see a sailing yacht with her mainsail up and a black cone, apex downwards, hoisted forward. What does the cone tell you?
options: She is engaged in fishing
She has gear extending more than 150 m
She is under sail and also being propelled by machinery
She is at anchor
questions.explanation: Rule 25(e) requires a vessel proceeding under sail and also propelled by machinery to show a cone, apex downwards, forward. She is then a power-driven vessel. Fishing is two cones apex together, anchored is a ball, and outlying fishing gear is a cone apex upwards.

questions.stem: A 9 m Canadian sailboat motor-sails up the Fraser River by day without showing a cone. Under the Canadian modification, is that a breach?
options: Yes, unless she is under 7 m
No, the cone is only required at night
No, in Canadian waters of a river (and other inland waters listed) a vessel under 12 m is not required to show the cone, though she may
Yes, every vessel motor-sailing must show the cone
questions.explanation: Rule 25(f) exempts vessels under 12 m in Canadian waters of a roadstead, harbour, river, lake or inland waterway from the motor-sailing cone, while allowing them to show it. The cone is a day signal, and the exemption is based on 12 m, not 7 m. She is still a power-driven vessel for the steering and sailing rules.

questions.stem: At night a 14 m sailboat is motor-sailing with her engine in gear. What lights should she show?
options: Red over green at the masthead plus sidelights
Sidelights and sternlight only, because her sails are up
A tricolour and an all-round white light
Power-driven lights: a masthead light, sidelights and a sternlight
questions.explanation: Under Rule 3 a sailing vessel is one under sail with machinery not being used, so with her engine propelling her she is power-driven and shows Rule 23 lights: masthead light, sidelights and sternlight (at 14 m the under-12 m all-round white option is not available). Sailing lights or red over green would wrongly tell others she is under sail alone.
